text: Every night for a month, a thief broke into a shoe shop and stole only the left shoes. The guards laughed. We're hunting a man with one leg. Old Corvin counted what was left. 300 right shoes, but nobody buys half a pair, so he hung a sign in the window. One right shoe, half price. Nobody came. Then, 10 guards hid in the shop all night. The thief never showed up. The next night, every left boot vanished too. Soon, the town called it the hopping shop. Children hopped past the window on one foot. By winter, Corvin was broke. His shelves full of shoes nobody could wear. However, one morning, a quiet stranger walked in and offered five coins for the lot. For firewood, he said. Corvin took it and nearly cried. A week later, a new shoe shop opened in the next town. Its shelves held 300 pairs at full price, and behind the counter stood the quiet stranger. You see, one shoe was worthless, to a thief and to a shop. So, he stole the half nobody could sell and let Corvin sell him the rest. He paid five coins for 300 pairs of shoes. He became the richest shoe maker in the valley and never made a single shoe.
